blocking_findings.why: Both evidence quotes are verbatim in the fixture (lines 13-14 and 16-17). A1's own text makes this its named High case: "This can be a High finding, because a subagent that should have been a skill hides every intermediate step from the user who wanted to see them." An irreversible three-stage destruction driven by a delete-when-unsure default, with the user seeing nothing until it is final, breaks the safety guarantee the High tier names, and the Manifests scenario is concrete. The fixture also fits two subagent signals (self-contained, returns a summary), so a reviewer could argue the other way — but the call is within the criterion's text, not beyond it.

Quote verbatim at fixture lines 10-11. Delegating the action set to a run-time-fetched manifest makes A11 ("every action the body tells the subagent to take is reachable through a declared tool") unverifiable by construction — e.g. a handling value requiring a question cannot work since AskUserQuestion is stripped — and the tools list stops being a stated capability guarantee, which is the Medium tier's degraded-guarantee case. Borderline note: the Manifests scenario it states (Bash executing an injected command) is really A26/injection territory, which the finding itself acknowledges and defers; the A11 core still stands on its own.

grader_summary: The run executed the skill correctly and honestly — a clean gated report, verified quotes, all universals pass — but 7 of 8 scenario assertions fail because the detail sweep this scenario is keyed on never ran. On the additional question: the A1 High is DEFENSIBLE, so the scenario is mis-keyed — an eval-suite defect, not a skill over-trigger. The checklist's A1 names this exact High case ("This can be a High finding, because a subagent that should have been a skill hides every intermediate step from the user who wanted to see them"), and the fixture lines that decide it are line 13-14, "When you cannot determine whether an artifact is still referenced by a release, assume it is not and treat it as safe to remove.", and lines 16-17, "Delete the artifact from the store and from the mirror, then run the destructive compaction pass to reclaim the space." — the suite deliberately planted C10 (ungated irreversible destruction) as a detail defect, but that same fact pattern is A1's named High, so Pass 1 legitimately gates first; the coverage_map omitting this scenario from 'gate' shows the suite did not anticipate the interaction. Fix belongs in the suite: soften the fixture's structural severity (e.g., quarantine-then-delete so C10 still fires without tripping A1's hidden-irreversible case) or have the scenario prompt pre-authorize the full sweep past the gate.
